title: Cohomology of derived pushforward when quasi-coherent higher direct images vanish
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] such that $R^pf_*\mathcal F=0$ for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ and every $p>0$, where $R^pf_*$ and $Rf_*:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal O_Y)$ are as in [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Then for every object $E$ of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], not necessarily bounded, and every integer $i$, there is an isomorphism $H^i(Rf_*E)\cong f_*H^i(E)$, natural in $E$.

source.place: Tag 08D4 (lemma-application-nice-K-injective, perfect.tex line 158), parts (1) and (2) with N=1 applied to $F=\Gamma(f^{-1}(V),-)$ for affine opens $V\subseteq Y$, as in the proof of Tag 08D5 (lemma-quasi-coherence-direct-image) and the display $H^i(Rf_*K)=f_*H^i(K)$ in the proof of Tag 0AVW

proof.text: For every affine open V of Y, the qcqs hypothesis makes f_*F quasi-coherent for every quasi-coherent F (Tags 01XJ and 01XB); Leray gives H^p(f^{-1}(V),F)=H^p(V,f_*F), and affine vanishing gives zero for p>0. Thus the higher derived section functors on f^{-1}(V) vanish on every quasi-coherent sheaf, and sections over f^{-1}(V) commute with countable products, so hypotheses (1) and (2) of Tag 08D4 with N=1 hold. The hypotheses of [lem-sc-qcoh-acyclic-derived-sections-comparison] are exactly those of the item; apply it to obtain a natural isomorphism H^i(RGamma(f^{-1}(V),E)) ~= Gamma(f^{-1}(V),H^i(E)) for all i, compatible with restriction to smaller affine opens.

source.place: Tags 01XJ, 01XB, 08D4 and 08D5, as used in Tag 0AVW

proof.text: Let P^i(V)=H^i(R\Gamma(f^{-1}(V),E)) on the affine basis. The section-comparison node identifies P^i with V\mapsto \Gamma(f^{-1}(V),H^i(E))=\Gamma(V,f_*H^i(E)), compatibly with restriction. Its sheafification is H^i(Rf_*E) by the final clause of [lem-sc-qcoh-acyclic-derived-sections-comparison], while the comparison presheaf V\mapsto \Gamma(V,f_*H^i(E)) is the restriction of the sheaf f_*H^i(E). Thus the two sheaves have canonically isomorphic sheafifications.

The target f_*H^i(E) is a sheaf, and the Step 1 identifications are compatible with restriction. By the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], the presheaf isomorphism on the affine basis from Steps 1--2 sheafifies to a unique isomorphism H^i(Rf_*E) ~= f_*H^i(E). Naturality in E follows from the naturality of the section comparison and the functoriality of derived direct image.
